title: Earth’s magnetic poles flip, the last time 780,000 years ago
body: Earth’s magnetic field is generated by churning molten iron in the outer core, and it isn’t fixed. Every so often north and south swap places; there have been at least 183 reversals in the last 83 million years, at irregular intervals. The most recent happened about 780,000 years ago, before which a compass would have pointed south. The evidence is locked in rocks: lava and new seafloor record the field’s direction as they cool, forming magnetic stripes.
